mcqs.question: Which of the following equations best represents a displacement reaction?
mcqs.explanation: In a displacement reaction a more reactive metal (Zn) displaces a less reactive metal (Cu) from its compound. Option A shows this. Option B is a double displacement reaction, C is a synthesis (combustion) reaction, and D is a decomposition reaction.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the role of relative reactivity in metal displacement reactions?

options.A: A metal higher in the reactivity series can displace a metal lower in the series from its compound.
options.B: A metal lower in the reactivity series can displace a metal higher in the series from its compound.
options.C: Reactivity does not influence whether a metal can displace another metal.
options.D: Only non‑metals participate in displacement reactions.

mcqs.answer: A metal higher in the reactivity series can displace a metal lower in the series from its compound.
mcqs.explanation: The reactivity series orders metals by their tendency to lose electrons. A more reactive metal (higher in the series) can replace a less reactive metal from its salt. Options B, C, and D contradict this principle.

mcqs.learning_point: Use metal reactivity to predict displacement
mcqs.question: Given the metals Zn and Cu, which one will displace the other from its aqueous salt solution?

options.A: Zn will displace Cu from CuSO4 solution.
options.B: Cu will displace Zn from ZnSO4 solution.
options.C: Neither metal can displace the other.
options.D: Both metals can displace each other.

mcqs.answer: Zn will displace Cu from CuSO4 solution.
mcqs.explanation: Zinc is higher than copper in the reactivity series, so it can displace copper from copper(II) sulfate. Copper cannot displace zinc because it is less reactive. Options B, C, and D are therefore incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which of the following reactions is a double displacement (metathesis) reaction?
mcqs.explanation: In a double displacement reaction, the cations and anions exchange partners. Option A shows Na⁺ swapping with Ba²⁺, forming BaSO₄ (a precipitate) and NaCl. Option B is a single displacement, C is decomposition, and D is synthesis.

mcqs.question: When aqueous solutions of lead(II) nitrate and potassium iodide are mixed, which observation confirms a precipitation reaction?

options.A: A yellow solid (PbI₂) forms in the mixture.
options.C: The solution remains clear and colourless.
options.D: The temperature of the mixture rises sharply.

mcqs.answer: A yellow solid (PbI₂) forms in the mixture.
mcqs.explanation: Lead(II) iodide is insoluble in water and appears as a yellow precipitate, indicating a precipitation reaction. Gas evolution, no visible change, or temperature rise are not characteristic of this specific reaction.

mcqs.question: A student places a clean piece of zinc metal into a solution of copper(II) sulfate. Which observation best confirms that a displacement reaction has occurred?

options.A: Copper metal deposits on the zinc surface and the blue colour of the solution fades.
options.B: Bubbles of hydrogen gas are seen rising from the solution.
options.C: No visible change occurs in the solution or on the zinc.
options.D: The solution becomes acidic and emits a pungent smell.

mcqs.answer: Copper metal deposits on the zinc surface and the blue colour of the solution fades.
mcqs.explanation: Zinc, being more reactive, displaces copper ions, causing copper metal to precipitate and the Cu²⁺ colour to disappear. Gas evolution, no change, or acidity are unrelated to this displacement process.

mcqs.question: A common misconception is that all metals react vigorously with water. Which statement correctly clarifies this misconception?

options.A: Only metals that are above hydrogen in the reactivity series react with water under normal conditions.
options.B: All metals react with water, but the reaction is always slow.
options.C: No metal reacts with water; observed reactions are due to impurities.
options.D: Metal reactivity with water depends solely on the temperature of the water.

mcqs.answer: Only metals that are above hydrogen in the reactivity series react with water under normal conditions.
mcqs.explanation: Metals higher than hydrogen (e.g., Na, K, Ca) react with water, while less reactive metals (e.g., Fe, Cu) do not under standard conditions. Options B, C, and D are inaccurate.

mcqs.learning_point: Use metal reactivity to predict displacement
mcqs.question: Given the reactivity series K > Ca > Na > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Cu > Ag > Au, what will happen when an iron strip is placed in a solution of copper(II) nitrate?

options.A: Copper metal will be deposited and iron ions will go into solution.
options.B: Iron metal will be deposited and copper ions will go into solution.
options.C: No displacement will occur because both metals are in the same solution.
options.D: Both iron and copper will dissolve completely.

mcqs.answer: Copper metal will be deposited and iron ions will go into solution.
mcqs.explanation: Iron is higher than copper in the reactivity series, so iron can displace copper from its nitrate, producing copper metal and Fe²⁺ ions. Options B, C, and D contradict the reactivity principle.
